programs.nl_rule: The input contains a two-color rectangle (one edge color and a different fill color) and a single light-blue marker outside it.  The output grid size stays the same. Stretch the rectangle only in the direction of the light-blue marker, stopping when its outer edge reaches the marker (inclusive so the rectangle’s edge is now at the height or width where the marker has been initially). Continue the rectangle's border color around the new outside edge and its inner color through the enlarged interior.

Let me understand the rule and the verifier.

The input has a rectangle with border color and fill color, and a single light-blue marker (8) outside it. Output stretches the rectangle in the direction of the marker until the rectangle's outer edge reaches the marker's row/column.

In the example: rectangle at rows 3-6, cols 2-4, border 1, fill 4. Marker 8 at row 3, col 6. So marker is to the right. The rectangle's right edge is at col 4. Stretch right until right edge reaches col 6. So new rectangle rows 3-6, cols 2-6. Border color 1 around new outside edge, fill 4 inside.

Output: rows 3-6, cols 2-6. Row 3: cols 2-6 = 1. Row 4: col 2=1, cols 3-5=4, col 6=1. Row 5 same. Row 6: cols 2-6=1. Yes matches.

Note: the marker cell at row 3 col 6 becomes the border color 1.

Now the verifier: it finds the rectangle (the object whose indices equal its box, i.e., filled rectangle... actually equality of toindices and box means the object is a solid rectangle outline? Wait box returns outline of patch. Hmm.

Let me re-read: x1 = fork(equality, toindices, box). So for each object (grouped by color via partition), check if toindices(obj) == box(obj). box(patch) returns outline of the bounding box. So an object equals its box when the object is exactly the outline of its bounding box. That's the border rectangle (color 1). x2 = multiply(height,width). x3 = fork(equality, size, x2) — size of object equals area of bbox. x4 = flip → not equal. x5 = both(x1, x4): object equals its own box AND size != area. Hmm, so the object is the outline (equals box) but its cell count differs from full area — that's a hollow rectangle (border). Yes! The border rectangle: its indices = box of itself, and size = perimeter < area. So x6 = the border rectangle object (color 1).

x7 = inbox(x6): inbox is the inner ring... Actually inbox returns the boundary of the inner region (one inside). x8 = backdrop(x7) = bounding box of inbox = the interior region (filled). x9 = toobject(x8, I) = the interior cells with their colors from I.

x10 = remove(x9, x0) — remove x9 from the set of all objects. x11 = remove(x6, x10) — remove border from that. x12 = argmin(x11, size) = smallest object among remainder = the marker (single cell, 8). x13 = combine(x12, x6) = marker + border rectangle. x14 = backdrop(x13) = bounding box covering both = the stretched rectangle bbox.

x15 = color(x9) = the fill color (from interior object). x16 = fill(I, x15, x14) — fill entire new bbox with fill color. x17 = color(x6) = border color. x18 = box(x14) = outline of new bbox. x19 = fill(x16, x17, x18) — fill outline with border color.

Great, so the rule: find border rectangle, find marker, take bounding box of both, fill with inner color, then outline with border color.

Important subtlety: The stretch direction. The bbox of marker + rectangle. If marker is directly right, bbox extends right only. If marker is diagonal? Probably not. The marker is aligned with a row or column of the rectangle (outside along one edge). Bbox naturally extends in whatever direction.

Wait uppermost=1, leftmost=1. ai=2, aj=2. bi,bj = lowermost-1, rightmost-1 = 2, 3. si,sj=min(2,2),min(2,3)=(2,2). ei,ej=max(2,2),max(2,3)=(2,3). vlines = {(i,2),(i,3) for i in range(2,3+1)} = {(2,2),(2,3),(3,2),(3,3)}. hlines similarly {(2,2),(2,3),(3,2),(3,3)}. So inbox = {(2,2),(2,3),(3,2),(3,3)}. good. backdrop = same bbox. good.

So should work... unless the issue is my grid uses height 9 which is fine.

Maybe the problem: the marker at (6,2) is within the column range of rectangle (cols1-4). When combined backdrop rows1-6 cols1-4 — fine.

Hmm, but maybe the issue is the marker being directly below and adjacent... no.

Let me reconsider whether the verifier requires the marker to be adjacent/outside with a gap? "single light-blue marker outside it". Mine is outside.

Maybe the error is actually that the input grid, when passed, throws because of the check that the rule applies — some verifiers have a precondition. But this verifier doesn't have explicit precondition.

Wait, maybe issue: x12 = argmin(x11, size). x11 = remove(x6, x10) where x10 = remove(x9,x0). If x9 (interior as object with value 3) is equal to color3 object, removed, leaving {bg0, marker8}. argmin size -> marker. Good.

But wait — what if there's no color3 separate object because... no.

Hmm, let me just test with the original teacher example shape to confirm the format. Actually the teacher example had a 5-wide? No: cols2-4 width3, border 1 fill4, marker 8 at (3,6) to the right. It worked (presumably). Let me replicate similar structure exactly: rectangle 3x3 with border and fill, marker to the right at some gap.

My failing case: maybe because rectangle width 4 and border top row all 7 including corners... that's standard.

Hmm, let me reconsider: maybe issue is marker color 8 appearing but the background? no.

content.text:
That worked. So the vertical failing case must have had a subtle issue. Interesting: in the failing vertical case, marker at (6,2). Rectangle rows1-3 cols1-4. But wait, notice marker column 2 is within rect columns. Direction is down. Hmm.

Actually wait, maybe the verifier requires the marker to share the exact column/row of the rectangle's edge? No.

Let me reconsider the failing case: rectangle rows1-3 (height3), cols1-4 (width4). Fill interior rows2 two rows of 3,3 -> wait I wrote:
row1: [0,7,7,7,7,0,...] cols1-4 all 7
row2: [0,7,3,3,7,0,...] cols1=7,2=3,3=3,4=7
row3: [0,7,3,3,7,...]
So rect rows1-3, cols1-4. border all 7, interior rows2-3 cols2-3 are 3s. That's a valid rectangle. Hmm.

Oh wait! The interior is 2 rows tall and 2 cols. inbox of rect: ai=2,aj=2, bi=blowermost-1=2, bj=rightmost-1=3. So inbox rows 2..2, cols2..3 -> {(2,2),(2,3)}. But actual interior of rect is rows2-3 (two rows), cols2-3. inbox only captured one row! Because inbox is defined as border shrunk by 1 on all sides; for a rectangle it gives cells from (top+1,left+1) to (bottom-1,right-1) as a ring, but backdrop of that is (top+1,left+1)-(bottom-1,right-1) bbox = correct interior bbox. inbox returns a ring though. Hmm inbox returns vlines|hlines of range(si,ei+1) with sj..ej. With si=ei=2, sj=2,ej=3: vlines={(2,2),(2,3)}, hlines={(2,2),(2,3)}. So inbox={(2,2),(2,3)}. backdrop bbox rows2-2 cols2-3. So x8 only covers row2 interior! Then x9=toobject only row2's two 3-cells. x10=remove(x9,x0): x9 = {(3,(2,2)),(3,(2,3))} which is NOT equal to full color3 object {(3,(2,2)),(3,(2,3)),(3,(3,2)),(3,(3,3))}. So removal fails! x10 stays x0. x11=remove(x6,x0)= {bg,fill,marker}. argmin size = marker. Still fine... x15 = color(x9)=3. x14 backdrop(marker+rect) rows1-6 cols1-4. fill 3, box 7. So output still fine. Hmm but it errored.

Wait but actually for a rectangle of height 3, top=1,bottom=3, top+1=2, bottom-1=2, so interior height 1, but actual interior is rows2 only? No: border is row1 and row3; interior row2 only! I wrote row2 and row3 both having 3s, but row3 is the bottom border (all 7s)? Let me recheck my grid:

Row3: [0,7,3,3,7,0,...] — I wrote cols1=7,2=3,3=3,4=7. So row3 has center 3s, not 7s! So the bottom border isn't complete. That's the bug — my grid wasn't a proper rectangle outline. Indeed row3 should be [0,7,7,7,7,...]. I mistakenly made fill 2x2 but the rectangle would be rows1-3 so interior only row2. My grid had an extra interior row, meaning the object isn't a rectangle outline.

So the failed queries were invalid rectangles. Fine, learned.

Now the current demonstration set: many. The student likely understands. Let me do one more probe with a fresh unseen valid instance, ideally vertical stretch done correctly, to verify.

Vertical stretch: rectangle rows4-6 cols2-4, marker above at (1,3). Proper rectangle: border 6, fill 9? Let's design.

row1: border top: 6 6 6 at cols2-4
rows2-5: 6 9 6
row6: 6 6 6

Let me query student this.

Wait, but is "stretch stopping when outer edge reaches marker" — marker at row1, rect top row4, so stretch upward until top at row1. Yes.
